subject.title: [RE-OPEN REQUEST] Indexing sync failure for jjr-iot-skill (Previous #2047)

question: Should maintainers restore public visibility for `janeXlab/jjr-iot-skill` after verifying the reporter's account, publisher ownership, latest version, scan, moderation, deletion, license, audit, and search-digest state?
rationale: The code path is security-sensitive and the decisive facts are private production state, so automation cannot safely choose between reindexing, restoring, keeping hidden, or asking for account verification.

options.title: Audit then restore if safe
options.body: Use operator/admin tooling to verify ownership and all public exposure gates, then restore or reindex through the existing publish/admin path if the skill is safe and authorized.

options.title: Keep hidden pending verification
options.body: Leave the skill unavailable and ask the reporter for account/login confirmation if ownership or account state cannot be verified.

options.title: Split a source fix only if systemic
options.body: Open a narrower code issue only if the audit shows a repeatable source bug in search/detail gate synchronization rather than a one-row production state problem.

recommendation.title: Audit then restore if safe
recommendation.body: Use operator/admin tooling to verify ownership and all public exposure gates, then restore or reindex through the existing publish/admin path if the skill is safe and authorized.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS and blame point to this handle for the central Convex API, skills, publishing, moderation, and scan surfaces involved in the visibility decision.
